newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lenders await new NZ govt before rate moves - REINZ.
newsitem.headline: Lenders await new NZ govt before rate moves - REINZ.

text.p: Home mortgage lenders appear to be awaiting a new coalition government, expected to be announced on Tuesday, before making any further changes to the level of rates, NZPA reported the Real Estate Institute (REINZ) as saying on Tuesday.
Mortgage interest rates have fallen since August, gathering pace in early November, particularly in the fixed rate market.
REINZ president Colin Brown said that lenders now appeared to be waiting to see the shape of a new government before making further decisions.
"Current speculation that a Labour-NZ First-Alliance (coalition) would raise pressure on financial markets has put a temporary halt to other lenders matching these lower rates," Brown said.
However, some commentators also believe that the Reserve Bank's monetary statement due on December 17 would be more important than politics, he said.

Commenting on recent mortgage interest rate moves, he said that by far the greatest number of interest rate drops had been among fixed term loans with 22 of 30 institutions surveyed reducing rates during the last month.
Brown said the lowest fixed rate on offer of 8.25 percent for six months was from a single lender.
But the most intense competition appeared to be in the two and three-year fixed loans with two lenders offering rates of 8.65 percent.
Rates for one-year fixed loans ranged between 8.80 percent and 9.95 percent. First mortgage floating rates ranged between 10.15 and 10.75 percent.
